subject: Post-incident: Finovista closure packet, verification steps, and action tracker
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Julia Park <julia.park@finovista.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Post-incident: Finovista closure packet, verification steps, and action tracker

Hi Julia —

Thanks again for your patience while we completed our internal review of last week's inference disruption. Attached is a compact closure packet we've prepared for Finovista. The packet includes: an executive RCA, a detailed minute-by-minute timeline, the action tracker with owners and deadlines, and a small log excerpt demonstrating the roaming PID error we addressed. Attachments: finovista_rca_summary_v1.pdf, action_tracker.xlsx, replay_logs_snippet.txt.

High-level summary (TL;DR):
- Root cause: a cascading scheduler bug in a backline GPU allocation path that allowed stale KV cache references for a subset of model variants, which increased CPU wait time and triggered request timeouts for long-conversation sessions.
- Impact window: Nov 18 02:47–03:26 UTC (see timeline in packet).
- Customer-facing effect: token generation latencies > 8s for ~2.1% of requests; elevated 429s for queued requests under contention.
- Mitigation taken: emergency config rollback + hotfix to allocation guard deployed at 03:40 UTC; follow-up patch rolled to stable fleet on Nov 19.

What we need from you to close out the ticket from a compliance perspective:
1) Confirmation that the packet and timeline meet Finovista's audit requirements (we can expand sections if you need additional evidence).
2) Indicate whether the log snippet and the monitoring dashboards suffice for your SRE/audit team or if you'd like full traces for specific request IDs (we can redact PII).
3) A short acceptance note from Finovista security when you are ready, or a list of follow-ups you want added to the action tracker.

Proposed verification plan:
- 2-week monitoring window: we will run enhanced telemetry for the affected routes and share daily summaries for 14 days.
- Joint verification call: propose Tue Nov 30, 10:00–10:30 PT to walk the packet and agree on closure items.

I've copied Marissa (CS) and Hannah (Head of Platform Reliability) so they can follow up with technical detail and long-term mitigations.

Next steps from our side (short):
- Share the full timeline and action tracker (attached) — DONE
- Enable extended telemetry for your account for 14 days — will start now
- Provide a redacted trace bundle for any request IDs you ask us to inspect — on request

If you'd like a shorter executive version for your compliance binder, say the word and we'll produce a one-page statement.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs:
- finovista_rca_summary_v1.pdf (18 pages: exec summary, timeline, root cause analysis, mitigations)
- action_tracker.xlsx (columns: item, owner, due_date, status, notes)
- replay_logs_snippet.txt (text excerpt: redacted request ids and stack traces)

From: Julia Park <julia.park@finovista.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Marco Rossi <m.rossi@finovista.com>, finovista-security@finovista.com
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-incident: Finovista closure packet, verification steps, and action tracker

Jonas —

Thanks for the packet and the quick turnaround. A couple of clarifying asks from our side before we mark this as closed with compliance: 
1) Can you provide guardrail evidence for the stable fleet patch you mentioned (Nov 19 deploy)? Specifically, the release ID and the canary metrics you used to roll that out.
2) We will need the raw traces for three example request IDs (we'll send the IDs separately) that show the end-to-end timing and any retry behavior; redaction is expected.
3) Please add a short section to the RCA that outlines the steps Redwood will take to prevent regressions in multi-tenant allocation logic — our auditors want an explicit regression mitigation plan.

Regarding the proposed verification call, Nov 30 at 10:00 PT works for Marco and me. We'll have two members of our security team on the call; I'll send the calendar invite.

Appreciate the clear next steps.

Julia Park
Head of SRE, Finovista
julia.park@finovista.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Julia Park <julia.park@finovista.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 14:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-incident: Finovista closure packet, verification steps, and action tracker

Hi Julia —

Thanks for the quick read and the pointed requests. Short answers and what we will deliver before the Nov 30 call: 
- Stable fleet patch evidence: I'll attach the release manifest and the canary dashboard snapshots (release ID: rel-20261119-3f7a). We'll include the percentage rollout timeline and key metrics (latency, error-rate).
- Raw traces for three request IDs: send the IDs in a separate email and we'll pull redacted bundles and the corresponding server-side logs. Suggestion: include one short session, one long conversation, and one retry path to capture variance.
- Regression mitigation write-up: Hannah is preparing a short plan outlining code-level guardrails (allocation guard, stricter KV cache lifecycle checks), additional automated tests added to our CI, and an ops runbook for emergency rollback criteria. We'll add that as an addendum to the RCA PDF.

Action items we'll complete before the call (also in the attached action_tracker.xlsx):
- Item 1: Add release manifest + canary snapshots — Owner: Marissa — Due: 2026-11-27 — Status: In progress
- Item 2: Redacted trace bundles for three request IDs — Owner: Platform Eng (Hannah) — Due: 2026-11-29 — Status: Pending
- Item 3: RCA addendum with regression mitigation plan — Owner: Hannah — Due: 2026-11-27 — Status: In progress
- Item 4: Start 14-day enhanced telemetry and share daily health summaries — Owner: Grace O'Connor (Monitoring Lead) — Due: start 2026-11-20 — Status: Active

If it's helpful, I can also include a short compliance checklist template Finovista can sign to indicate acceptance (one-line acceptance + optional notes).

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachment stubs included in this message: release_manifest_rel-20261119-3f7a.json (redacted), canary_dashshots.zip (3 images)

Julia/Marco —

Appreciate the details and the alignment for the call on Nov 30. Quick confirmation of the checklist and owners so everything is explicit ahead of the meeting: 

Pre-call deliverables (we will deliver these items and drop links into the calendar invite):
- Release manifest + canary snapshots (Marissa) — done/attached to the call invite by 2026-11-27
- RCA addendum: regression mitigation + CI tests summary (Hannah) — draft by 2026-11-27
- Redacted trace bundles for the three request IDs you send (Platform Eng / Hannah) — delivered by 2026-11-29
- Daily 14-day telemetry summaries (Grace) — first summary sent 2026-11-21, ongoing through 2026-12-04
- Action tracker with explicit acceptance column for Finovista sign-off (Jonas/Marissa) — updated and shared before the meeting

Post-call closure criteria (what will count as "closed" from Redwood's side):
1) Finovista confirms the packet + addendum meet audit requirements (acceptance note or signed checklist).
2) No new regressions observed in the enhanced telemetry window for the affected routes.
3) Outstanding action items either completed or assigned with agreed timelines that Finovista accepts.

If Finovista prefers a short signed statement for its compliance binder we will prepare a single-page signed confirmation describing the incident, actions taken, and monitoring commitments.

Forwarded for convenience below is my original message and the attached stubs.
